title: SPACEMESHER source registry
purpose: Inventory of known public source catalogues, scientific archives and terrain generators that can contribute space-related 3D geometry. This is a discovery register, not a claim that every source has already been harvested.
completenessPrinciple: Track each source separately from imported records. Record its published scope, access method, licence/provenance requirements, import status and next action. Never treat a linked catalogue page or a terrain generator as an individually imported model.

statusDefinitions.indexed: A source index is already present in this repository; coverage may still be partial.
statusDefinitions.partial: Some objects or files are represented, but the source has a larger catalogue or unimported variants.
statusDefinitions.linked: The source is linked in the UI or documentation, but its contents are not systematically indexed.
statusDefinitions.candidate: A relevant public source discovered during source inventory; compatibility and harvesting method still need assessment.

spacecraft.scope: Spacecraft, satellites, probes, landers, rovers, crewed vehicles, stations, instruments and mission hardware.

sources.name: NASA 3D Resources
sources.knownCoverage: Repository index contains 650 unique NASA source files (679 index placements including 29 cross-listed planetary STL records). Of 226 NASA 3D Models folders, 221 now have verified individual NASA detail pages; five remain unresolved.
sources.nextAction: Recheck the five unresolved model folders for official individual detail pages and keep source-page URLs separate from direct file URLs.

sources.name: Space Radar Models and map assets
sources.type: downloadable model catalogue and map asset collection
sources.knownCoverage: Repository index contains 311 assets across spacecraft, small bodies and moons: 234 have a verified model-specific source page (Space Radar or the original PDS record); 77 map/composite assets currently have no verified individual source page and therefore remain without a source-page URL in their model records.
sources.nextAction: Reconcile the 77 map/composite asset credits against their original NASA/PDS records; add a model source link only when the exact original object page is verified.

sources.name: models.codelove.in — Space collection
sources.knownCoverage: Live catalogue reports 586 space models in 10 collections; Satellites & Probes collection reports about 180 models. Public-domain/CC0 claims must be checked per item.
sources.nextAction: Inspect catalogue API and enumerate records, categories, file URLs and per-model licence metadata.

sources.name: ESA Science Satellite Fleet (Sci-Fleet)
formats: 3D web assets; downloadable formats to verify
sources.knownCoverage: Catalogue lists ESA science missions including ARIEL, BepiColombo, Cassini-Huygens, Euclid, Gaia, Hubble, JUICE, Mars Express, Rosetta and others.
sources.nextAction: Inspect download controls/network assets and determine which models are legally and technically retrievable.

sources.name: ESA Satellite Models
sources.knownCoverage: ESA education resource presents printable satellite models, including CHEOPS.
sources.nextAction: Enumerate individual models and check source files and reuse terms.

sources.name: NASA/JPL Cosmographia
sources.knownCoverage: Scientific visualisation ecosystem using SPICE-enhanced Solar System geometry and mission models.
sources.nextAction: Identify distributable mesh/DSK assets and distinguish model geometry from ephemeris and visualisation packages.

planetary.scope: Planetary landforms, craters, mountains, valleys, volcanoes, surface regions and derived terrain meshes.

sources.name: NASA Solar System Treks
sources.type: surface data portal and on-demand terrain generator
sources.knownCoverage: Portals cover planets, moons and asteroids. NASA documents pre-generated whole-globe print files for Bennu, Ceres, Ryugu and Vesta; users can select local features for 3D printing.
sources.nextAction: Enumerate every portal, available terrain export, whole-body print file and supported map layer. Treat user-generated regions as generator outputs, not pre-existing catalogue records.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia
sources.knownCoverage: Planetary maps, mosaics and elevation/cartographic products across multiple bodies.
sources.nextAction: Search and enumerate DEM and topographic products separately from image-only map products.

sources.name: USGS Map-a-Planet
sources.knownCoverage: Selects global or regional image mosaics from Astropedia and exports processed map imagery; not itself a 3D mesh catalogue.
sources.nextAction: Assess whether output imagery can be paired with elevation data to create reproducible terrain models.

sources.name: NASA PDS Geosciences Node
sources.knownCoverage: Includes lunar LOLA, GRAIL, Apollo, Kaguya, Clementine, Mercury MESSENGER, Mars and other mission holdings; selected products include high-resolution topography and DEMs.
sources.nextAction: Build a product-level inventory of usable DEMs and elevation grids, with body, resolution, coordinate system and licence.

sources.name: Terrain Print
formats: STL or generated mesh; verify current exports
sources.knownCoverage: Generator for terrain from elevation data; not a static model library.
sources.nextAction: Document supported input sources, export formats and limits; keep separate from indexed model counts.

sources.name: NASA 3D Resources — planetary assets
sources.knownCoverage: NASA index already includes planetary feature and surface-related files, but many NASA entries are spacecraft or generic mission objects.
sources.nextAction: Reclassify NASA files using source metadata and identify all actual surface-feature geometry.

small-bodies.scope: Asteroids, comets, dwarf planets, meteoroids and meteorite specimens; preserve separate object identity and every available shape-model variant.

sources.name: 3D Asteroid Catalogue
sources.knownCoverage: Source reports 1,635 asteroids, 5 comets, 2 dwarf planets, 37 moons, 3,079 shape models and 54 textures. SPACEMESHER currently has 256 numbered asteroid catalogue references, all 5 comet pages, both dwarf-planet pages (Ceres and Pluto), and 37 individually indexed moon catalogue references. Object-level direct file variants are still incomplete.
sources.nextAction: Harvest all asteroid object pages and every model variant; verify individual comet, dwarf-planet and moon detail URLs and direct file endpoints rather than treating parent catalogue links as downloads.

sources.name: NASA PDS Small Bodies Node — asteroid data sets
sources.knownCoverage: Archive lists Bennu, Vesta, Ceres, Eros, Itokawa, Phobos, Mimas, Dione, Tethys, Phoebe, Lutetia, Steins, Arrokoth and multiple optical/radar model collections.
sources.nextAction: Enumerate every shape/DTM product and download individual meshes where directly available; keep source dataset and model variants distinct.

sources.name: PDS SBN Small Body Optical Shape Models (Thomas)
sources.knownCoverage: Includes Ida, Gaspra, Mathilde, Vesta, Phobos, Deimos, Hyperion, Janus and Epimetheus.
sources.nextAction: Extract and catalogue each body model and its variants from the PDS4/PDS3 bundle.

sources.name: PDS SBN Small Body Radar Shape Models (Hudson)
sources.knownCoverage: Includes Kleopatra, Geographos, Bacchus, Toutatis, Castalia, Golevka, 1998 KY26, 52760 and Itokawa.
sources.nextAction: Extract and catalogue every model and resolution from the bundle.

sources.name: PDS SBN Stooke Small Body Shape Models
sources.knownCoverage: Includes Ida, Mathilde, Gaspra, comet Halley and moons Amalthea, Thebe, Larissa, Proteus, Janus, Epimetheus, Prometheus and Pandora.
sources.nextAction: Extract all individual body meshes; classify comet and asteroid objects here, moons under the Moons category, while retaining common source provenance.

sources.name: NASA PDS Rosetta 67P Shape Models V2.0
sources.knownCoverage: Contains multiple Rosetta OSIRIS and NAVCAM shape models; dataset was updated with additional SPG and SPC models in 2026.
sources.nextAction: Enumerate all model products and reference frames; compare with the 3D Asteroid Catalogue to preserve distinct variants.

sources.name: NASA/JPL Radar Astronomy Shape Models
sources.knownCoverage: Repository index contains 19 direct OBJ records. The official JPL source presents the models in one catalogue list with individual OBJ download links; no separate per-model detail pages were identified.
sources.nextAction: Continue monitoring the JPL shape-model list; keep individual source-page links unset unless a dedicated model detail page becomes available.

sources.name: JAXA DARTS — Itokawa Gaskell Shape Model
sources.knownCoverage: Public directory contains multiple numbered STL, TRI and TXT model files for asteroid Itokawa.
sources.nextAction: Enumerate all model resolutions and document units, coordinate frame and conversion requirements.

sources.name: JAXA DARTS — Hayabusa2 Ryugu Shape Models
sources.knownCoverage: Published Ryugu shape variants include 3M, 800k, 200k and 49k polygon OBJ models; JADE2 links global DSK shape models.
sources.nextAction: Enumerate official downloadable variants and preserve their resolution lineage.

sources.name: NASA Astromaterials 3D
sources.knownCoverage: Apollo lunar samples and Antarctic meteorites; current repository includes 17 linked Antarctic meteorite sample pages, not the complete collection.
sources.nextAction: Enumerate all sample records and retrieve sample-specific full/low-resolution OBJ downloads and metadata. Keep lunar samples cross-listed with lunar material rather than classifying them as asteroids.

sources.name: Zenodo — NWA 869 and rock-fragment meshes
sources.knownCoverage: Repository links the exact Zenodo record DOI 10.5281/zenodo.14850374 and three archives: L01.zip (199.8 MB), L02.zip (197.6 MB) and T01.zip (56.8 MB). Together the dataset reports 868 OBJ meshes; L01/L02 are NWA 869 meteorite fragments, T01 contains terrestrial rock fragments.
sources.nextAction: Resolve DOI and dataset files, enumerate meshes and separate extraterrestrial specimens from terrestrial comparison material.

moons.scope: Natural satellites as astronomical bodies and their global or regional shape models; not spacecraft sent to moons.

sources.name: 3D Asteroid Catalogue — moons
sources.knownCoverage: Source reports 37 moons; repository currently has 13 Moon-category records across NASA and Space Radar indexes, with the 37-object listing not yet fully imported.
sources.nextAction: Enumerate all 37 moon records and all shape-model variants; compare with PDS holdings.

sources.name: NASA PDS Ring-Moon Systems Node
sources.knownCoverage: Archives data for Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto systems; OPUS supports searching surface geometry and PDS bundles include moon/ring products.
sources.nextAction: Identify all distributable satellite shape models and surface topography products; filter out image-only and geometry metadata products.

sources.name: PDS SBN Saturn Satellite Shape Models
sources.knownCoverage: SBN archive lists Saturn satellite shape-model collections including Gaskell models of Dione, Mimas, Phoebe and Tethys, plus Stooke/Thomas moon models.
sources.nextAction: Extract every satellite mesh and version into the Moons category, with original dataset IDs.

sources.name: PDS SBN Optical Shape Models — planetary satellites
sources.knownCoverage: Includes Phobos, Deimos, Hyperion, Janus and Epimetheus.
sources.nextAction: Cross-list moon records from the common optical shape model bundle without duplicating the underlying source file.

sources.name: PDS SBN Stooke Shape Models — satellites
sources.knownCoverage: Includes Amalthea, Thebe, Larissa, Proteus, Janus, Epimetheus, Prometheus and Pandora.
sources.nextAction: Cross-list every individual moon mesh in Moons while retaining source dataset and version.

sources.name: NASA Solar System Treks — Moons
sources.type: interactive surface portal and terrain export
sources.knownCoverage: Portals include Earth's Moon, Phobos, Europa, Ganymede, Io, Callisto, Titan and Icy Moons Treks.
sources.nextAction: Inventory downloadable whole-body/region geometry and supported exports for each moon portal.

height-maps.scope: Elevation grids, DEMs, topographic rasters and derived printable terrain meshes for planets, moons and small bodies.

sources.name: NASA Solar System Treks — elevation and 3D print
sources.knownCoverage: Surface portals include Moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, Titan, Icy Moons, Phobos, Europa, Ganymede, Io, Callisto, Bennu, Ceres, Ryugu and Vesta. Whole-globe print files are explicitly documented for Bennu, Ceres, Ryugu and Vesta.
sources.nextAction: Inventory each body's available elevation products and downloadable print geometry; distinguish global DEMs from local regions.

sources.name: NASA PDS Geosciences Node — topography and DEM holdings
sources.knownCoverage: Mission holdings include lunar LOLA, GRAIL, Kaguya, Clementine and South Pole DEM products, plus Mars and Mercury data.
sources.nextAction: Enumerate actual DEM products, resolution, coverage, vertical datum, coordinate system and file access.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia — elevation and topography products
sources.type: planetary map and elevation data catalogue
sources.knownCoverage: Planetary cartographic archive; product availability and elevation-vs-imagery distinction must be checked per record.
sources.nextAction: Query all planetary DEM/topography products and record direct data links and metadata.

sources.name: NASA PDS Ring-Moon Systems Node — satellite topography
sources.knownCoverage: Outer-planet systems archive includes geometry, ring and moon datasets; usable elevation products need product-level verification.
sources.nextAction: Search for actual elevation grids and DTM products, not just surface imagery or SPICE kernels.

sources.name: Terrain Print
formats: STL or generated mesh; verify current exports
sources.knownCoverage: Converts elevation sources into printable terrain; generator rather than an independent elevation-data source.
sources.nextAction: Record as a preparation tool, not as a source of new planetary DEMs.

auditNotes: NASA 3D Resources and Space Radar are already indexed, but their category counts must not be confused with counts of unique celestial objects.
The 3D Asteroid Catalogue's published counts are source-reported and include 37 moons, 3,079 shape models and textures; current SPACEMESHER records are only a subset.
NASA PDS SBN has multiple distinct optical, radar, Stooke, comet and mission-specific shape-model datasets; each dataset may contain multiple body meshes and model variants.
NASA Solar System Treks is primarily a scientific surface-data portal and generator. It is not equivalent to a static downloadable model catalogue.
NASA Astromaterials 3D contains scanned lunar and meteorite specimens; specimens must not be conflated with whole-body asteroid/moon shape models.
Source inventory intentionally includes candidate sources that still need format, licence, direct-download and completeness checks.
